scope: Read-only implementation/design review; no test/model run; no runtime source edits.

candidate.execution_scope: serial text, MTP off, residency enabled

recommendation: Proceed as a bounded applicability-policy candidate, not a proven root-cause correction or an additional long-prefill speedup.
methodology: 8192 is chosen using earlier failed short-tier results and aligns with the frozen prefill chunk size; disclose this training-on-prior-results fact.
Retain the previous full-range candidate NO_GO as an unchanged historical result.

Formal new candidate comparison is same-binary legacy partition off versus request policy on; comparing only against previously rejected full-range min_new does not establish acceptance relative to legacy.
Freeze all thresholds, challenge inputs, sequence order, stop rules and sample counts before tests; do not expand after favorable or unfavorable performance.
No evidence presently supports broad non-regression for every length above 8192, all text tasks, or arbitrary request histories.
A formal pass would qualify the already observed long-context benefit for the tested policy; it would not prove another 10–20 percent prefill reduction.

critical_contracts.requirement: Choose policy from complete tokenized/expanded input once; carry immutable full length, request ID and derived chunk base through request thread, scheduler, Model, DecoderLayer and MoE.

ModelPrefillTextChunk continuation goes through ModelDecodeBatch, also used for MTP verify. Explicit policy must reach it without enabling policy for MTP/decode calls. Check base, full length and range; singleton tail remains real prefill.

Prefer an explicit value context. If stored in sequence state, Begin/End and failed/cancelled reuse must reset/refreeze it. Never use process mutable environment or thread_local to select per request.
Cover queued singleton prefill, requeued chunk prefill, and scheduler-inactive inline fallback. Policy must outlive worker execution and be preserved through each requeue.

Reject enabled unsupported max_seq>1, MTP, media and nonresidency at server startup; non-HTTP APIs without request context retain documented existing global behavior, never infer full length from current T.
Policy off preserves global partition semantics; policy on requires global partition=1 and chunk_order=0. Invalid or conflicting values reject before model load. Log the effective policy.
A short request using legacy still inherits GPU/L2/mirror/Linux cache state from prior long requests. No implicit cache reset, metadata restore or hidden prewarming is allowed.
critical_contracts.evidence: ModelBeginSequence resets recurrent state, not MoEResidency; OFFLOAD_DIAGNOSTICS_2026-10-04.md:199–220

acceptance_coverage: First actual test remains fixed tools/evalscope HTTP quality on the new binary; host/numerical checks follow.
Host coverage: strict parsing/truth table, thresholds 8192/8193, immutable full length and chunk-base validation, false/default context, request identity, cancellation/reuse ownership.
HTTP challenge boundary: 8192 and 8193, including long first chunk 8192 and singleton tail 1; add a predeclared middle length such as 16385 to challenge two full chunks plus singleton tail.
Preserve normal five tiers plus capacity target and same 16GiB host/cache settings. Disable diagnostic instrumentation in formal performance runs.
Explicit fixed long-to-short request sequence in one service is required to assess history risk; normal ascending six tiers does not cover it.

Current-binary true-weight numerical checks should cover legacy versus min_new layer output/router/FP32 contracts including singleton/noncontiguous scatter. Existing unchanged planner evidence can be cited as prior limited evidence, not wholesale certification of the new binary.
Runtime cancellation/load-failure and subsequent opposite-policy request need coverage if accepting lifecycle behavior. HTTP output equality alone does not prove internal numerical equality.
Same schema reason=decode historically denoted T==1. New request-policy logs should explicitly identify prefill_singleton instead of conflating shape and phase.

conditional_mirror_candidate.eligibility: Only a separately frozen phase after request policy conclusion; do not bundle into the current candidate.
conditional_mirror_candidate.motivation: Diagnostic 8K candidate prefill had about 36,726 mirror writebacks but only about 206 mirror hits out of 37,589 GPU loads. This identifies substantial low-reuse traffic, not an exposed critical-path or TTFT bound.
conditional_mirror_candidate.minimal_safe_control: An explicit actual-prefill writeback policy carried on LoadPlan into StageTask/CommitExpert can skip the optional victim D2H writeback while preserving mirror reads, event waits, claims, immutable payload identities and ring bookkeeping for entries actually present. Do not change mirror_k at runtime or reset IDs/events to fake a cold cache.
conditional_mirror_candidate.scope_choice_to_freeze: Either all prefill writebacks off or nonfinal prefill chunks off with final chunk unchanged is a distinct candidate. The latter protects some decode handoff behavior but does not reproduce legacy terminal cache state; singleton final chunks are an important challenge. Select only one before testing.
conditional_mirror_candidate.why_not_decode_phase_flag: LoadPlan.decode_phase currently reflects singleton subchunk shape and is contaminated by prefill singletons; it cannot select actual prefill policy safely.
proof_obligations: Existing immutable cached expert payload remains valid when a later writeback is skipped; preserve source-buffer claims through H2D and event recording.
No writeback ring target may be repurposed while a pending H2D reads it; no GPU slot overwrite may race a GEMM.
Measure extra storage reads, increased miss costs, final cache state and all-tier decode instead of using low hit rate alone as success.
Final numerical, HTTP quality, full performance, cancellation and fault contracts remain necessary for an accepted runtime change.

do_not_do: No stream decoupling without slot lifetime ownership
No claim of strict total physical RAM from memcg or summed NVIDIA/RSS counters
remaining: Review final implementation diff after runtime agent completes; this file is a preimplementation design review, not an approval of unreviewed code.
